ResearchProjectDef.label: vacuumize process
ResearchProjectDef.description: Material production in vacuum effectively avoids interference from common gases such as nitrogen and oxygen during chemical reactions. Researching materials science outside the atmosphere is especially valuable for special materials like Tantasteel, which are prone to oxidation when processed in atmospheric conditions.\n\nThis research unlocks Tantasteel production in vacuum-compatible box furnaces and sintering furnaces.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Radar
ResearchProjectDef.description: Early detection and fire control in the style of the last great industrial war: concrete acoustic mirrors that listen for engines, a hand-cranked fire-control set that guides one interceptor at a time, and the first guided interceptor rockets.\n\nThis research unlocks the passive acoustic radar, the early fire control radar, the rotary launch rail, the legacy loitering munition and the legacy interceptor loitering munition.

ResearchProjectDef.label: loitering munition
ResearchProjectDef.description: Rail-launched pulsejet loitering munitions give an early colony a crude beyond-visual-range strike capability. Slow and easy to detect, but available long before proper cruise missiles.\n\nThis research unlocks the launch rail, the loitering munition rack and the strike planning table. With microelectronics basics, it also unlocks the long-range loitering munition.

ResearchProjectDef.label: orbital dynamics
ResearchProjectDef.description: By studying fundamental orbital mechanics and space environmental characteristics, you can develop equipment and precision devices designed for vacuum microgravity conditions, as well as a family of specialized caseless firearms built from advanced materials.\n\nKey materials and components for this equipment rely on trade with the colonial fleet, but deeper research can eventually enable fully independent production.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Carbon synthesis
ResearchProjectDef.description: Industrial-scale organic reactions can convert carbon dioxide and water into organic biomass. This "turn air into food" technology reached commercial viability before World War III, with energy conversion efficiency roughly eight to thirty times that of traditional agriculture.\n\nThis research unlocks construction of a bioreactor that consumes electricity and graphene to synthesize carbohydrates composed of starches, sugars, and other organic compounds.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Microgravity Manufacturing
ResearchProjectDef.description: Additive manufacturing in microgravity can achieve complexity and precision far beyond what is possible under gravity. Once gravity is removed as a constant constraint, many fundamental assumptions in materials science and manufacturing are significantly altered.\n\nThis research unlocks construction of a large assembly machine for producing items in microgravity.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Aerospace Applications
ResearchProjectDef.description: By scaling up Tantasteel and graphene production and exploring the key applications of these specialty materials in aerospace and microelectronics, this research unlocks nuclear thermal propulsion engines and orbital electronic-warfare stealth equipment for gravships and orbital starships, as well as the phased-array radar and the advanced air-defence gun.

ResearchProjectDef.label: ballistics
ResearchProjectDef.description: Systematic study of in-atmosphere missile flight dynamics, liquid- and solid-fuel staging and launch structures. The first ballistic rockets, manned rotary launchers and crew-served flak give a colony long-range fires without any electronics industry.\n\nThis research unlocks the ballistic launch tower and the legacy ballistic missile, the legacy flak gun, the tilt-launch container and a missile rack.

ResearchProjectDef.label: integrated circuits
ResearchProjectDef.description: High-density integrated electronics allow miniaturised signal processing and strapdown inertial reference units compact enough to fit inside a missile airframe. The result is a beyond-visual-range combat network with search radar, multi-channel fire-control radar and surface-to-air missile defence.\n\nThis research unlocks the search radar, the fire control radar, the field air-defence system, the SAM launcher, the man-portable SAM launcher, the light vertical launch cell, the light surface-to-air, field air-defence, ground-attack and advanced general-purpose missiles, the interceptor missile and the tactical ballistic missile.

ResearchProjectDef.label: strategic systems
ResearchProjectDef.description: Mastery of re-entry physics, high-energy propellant chemistry, and stellar-inertial guidance enables ballistic missiles that loft their payload to the edge of the atmosphere, and the same electronics give a new generation of low-observable and semi-active missiles. The ballistic arc defeats most point defences and allows strikes at extreme range with any assembled warhead configuration.\n\nThis research unlocks the strategic missile silo, the vertical launch silo, the current and strategic ballistic missiles, the thermonuclear warhead, and the advanced surface-to-air and subsonic cruise missiles.

ResearchProjectDef.label: anti-ship missiles
ResearchProjectDef.description: Active radar seekers that keep re-aiming at a moving target, sea-skimming flight profiles and ramjet propulsion turn missiles into weapons against ships and every other base that moves across the world map.\n\nThis research unlocks the anti-ship loitering munition and the tilt launch tube; integrated circuits are also required for the supersonic anti-ship missile, and strategic systems for the hypersonic anti-ship missile.
